hamlet.note: Whole work. Seminar VI, Desire and its Interpretation, 1958-59

antigone.note: Extracted from The Oedipus Trilogy, F. Storr translation. Seminar VII, The Ethics of Psychoanalysis, 1959-60

oedipus_rex.note: Extracted from The Oedipus Trilogy, F. Storr translation. Referred to throughout the Seminars

oedipus_at_colonus.note: Extracted from The Oedipus Trilogy, F. Storr translation. Seminar VII, on the boundary between life and death

electra.note: Extracted from The Seven Plays in English Verse, Lewis Campbell translation. Quoted in Seminar VII on Ate

awakening_of_spring.note: Whole play, Francis J. Ziegler translation. Preface a L'Eveil du printemps, 1 September 1974, in Autres ecrits p. 561

king_lear.note: Whole work. Modernised spelling, matching the other three Shakespeare plays. PG 1128, the First Folio old-spelling text used previously, is not comparable with them

medea.note: Whole play, Gilbert Murray verse translation

the_cherry_orchard.note: Extracted from Plays by Chekhov, Second Series, Constance Garnett translation

miss_julie.note: Extracted from Plays by August Strindberg, Second Series, Edwin Bjorkman translation. Titled Miss Julia in this translation

prometheus_bound.note: Extracted from Prometheus Bound and The Seven Against Thebes, Theodore Alois Buckley translation. Chosen as the Real at its limit: a subject fixed in place, addressing what cannot answer

agamemnon.note: Whole play, Gilbert Murray translation, the same translator as Medea and The Bacchae. Chosen as the Symbolic at its limit: every character positioned by house, oath, rank and debt

the_bacchae.note: Whole play, Gilbert Murray translation. Chosen for entropy: a play whose action is the dissolution of a coherent subject

ghosts.note: Whole work, R. Farquharson Sharp translation. Chosen for the trauma ratchet: inherited damage that never discharges

the_wild_duck.note: Whole play, Eleanor Marx Aveling translation. Chosen for the Imaginary, and as a same-author control against Ghosts

the_stronger.note: Extracted from Plays by August Strindberg, Second Series, Edwin Bjorkman translation. Chosen as the dyadic test for B3: two characters, one of whom never speaks

philoctetes.note: Extracted from The Seven Plays in English Verse, Lewis Campbell translation, the same volume and translator as Electra. Chosen for sustained physical pain as a state the calculus must carry, and as a translation control against Electra

everyman.note: Extracted from Everyman, with Other Interludes. Chosen as the negative control: allegorical figures are not subjects, and a calculus of subjectivity should register that or be wrong
